narr: The remnants of TS Beryl combined with deep tropical moisture and a stationary front draped across the region produced multiple rounds of heavy showers and storms. This led to numerous reports of flash flooding, some locally severe across portions of eastern New York, mainly in Essex County.
ev: Dept. of Highways and Emergency Management reported several roads washed out in the Keene/Keene Valley area of Essex County due to excessive rainfall of 2 to 4 inches. These included, but were not limited to Route 9N between Keene and Elizabethtown, and Route 73 in Keene Valley at Johns Brook.

Dept. of Highways and Emergency Management reported several roads damaged and/or washed out in and around the Elizabethtown, NY area due to 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. These included, but were not limited to Lincoln Pond Rd. and Route 9N between US 9 and Old Military Rd.

State Emergency Mgmt. reported several road washouts in and near the vicinity of New Russia, NY due to 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. These included, but were not limited to Roaring Brook Rd., Simonds Hill Rd. and Scriver Rd.

Dept. of Highways and Emergency Mgmt. reported several roads damaged and/or washed out in and in the vicinity of Westport, NY due to 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. These included, but were not limited to NY Route 22 between Main St. and Walker Rd., Route 9N, Ledge Hill Rd. and Lake Shore Rd.

Dept. of Highways and Emergency Management reported several roads closed and/or damaged due to high water/flash flooding as a result of 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. These included, but were not limited to NY Route 9, Stevenson Rd. and Bigelow Rd.

Emergency Mgmt. reported several roads flooded and/or damaged by flash flooding in and in the vicinity of Port Henry, NY due to 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. These included, but were not limited to Tunnel Ave. and Dock Lane.

Dept. of Highways reported several roads washed out or damaged in and near the vicinity of North Hudson, NY due to 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. This included, but was not limited to US Route 9 between Duntley Rd. and Tracy Rd.

Dept. of Highways and Emergency Management reported numerous roads closed and/or damaged due to flash flooding as a result of 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall. These included, but were not limited to Joyce Rd., Riddle Rd., Bridal Row Rd., the intersection of Witherbee and Tracy Roads, Pilfershire Rd. and Cheney Rd.
Emergency Mgmt. reported several roads washed out in the southern portions of Moriah, NY due to 2 to 4 inches of excessive rainfall. This included, but was not limited to Fairy Lake Rd.
The public reported that Route 11 was closed due to flash flooding in Ellenburg Depot, NY.
